headline: DA Pulls MP From Finance Role Over R4bn Probe
script: Big political U-turn in Parliament! DA MP Mark Burke — the party's own finance boss — has been yanked off Parliament's finance committees. Why? His fintech company Kastelo is accused by the Reserve Bank of moving about R4 billion offshore, allegedly using ordinary clients' foreign investment allowances without them even knowing. One example: clients earning R15,000 a month were given loans of R249,000 just to max out their allowances. A Johannesburg court already sided with the Reserve Bank, dismissing Kastelo's bid to unfreeze its accounts. The DA initially defended Burke, then reversed course a day later, replacing him with Kingsley Wakelin. The ANC says removing him doesn't end the accountability question. Why care? This is the guy who oversaw the Reserve Bank — while his own company was allegedly breaking its rules. That's exactly the kind of conflict of interest that affects trust in who's watching your money.
why_it_matters: It shows why conflicts of interest in Parliament's financial watchdog committees matter directly to how your money and the economy are protected.
